messages:
Sean (Acme): Hey team, multiple users in our app started seeing OAuth failures when signing in with Google around 09:12 UTC. Error in console is `invalid_grant` and server logs show `state_mismatch`. Works for some users but not others. We didn't change app config. Can you help?

Maya (support): Thanks Sean — can you paste the redirect_uri your app is sending and the exact error payload from your callback handler? Also, any recent infra changes (CDN, proxy)?

Sean (Acme): Redirect URI we have configured in GCP: `https://app.acme.com/auth/callback`
Callback request (anonymized):
```
{"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Mismatched state"}
```
We use Cloudflare Workers as an edge proxy that rewrites some paths to `/lite/*` for mobile clients. No config changes in the app itself.

Maya (support): Ok. Can you reproduce with curl and include the full redirect that Google sends back (the query string after the redirect)? Often state gets URL-encoded/truncated through proxies.

Sean (Acme): I tried a repro — clicking Google sign-in redirects to our CF worker URL: `https://edge.acme.com/lite/auth/callback?code=4/0AX4X...&state=2a8f3b0e...` but by the time it hits our origin the `state` param is shortened to `2a8f3`. So the oauth server rejects it.

Ravi (eng-auth): That sounds like the worker or a router rewriting/shortening querystring. Two quick checks: 1) Are we using URL.hash vs query? 2) Any header-based rewriting or NDJSON logging that truncates long query params?

Sean (Acme): The state is base64url-encoded PKCE+session nonce, usually ~128 chars. Works for desktop where we go straight to `app.acme.com`, but mobile flows go via `edge.acme.com/lite/`.

Leah (security): Common failure: some edge proxies impose max URL length or normalizers and can drop characters if you have a middleware that parses querystring as form-data and truncates. Also check if `?` vs `#` is being used. Google uses query param by default for web flow.

Maya (support): Could you share CF Worker script snippet (if safe) that does the rewrite? Even pseudo-code helps.

Sean (Acme): Worker snippet (redacted):
```
addEventListener('fetch', event => {
  let url = new URL(event.request.url);
  if (url.pathname.startsWith('/lite/')) {
    // strip prefix and proxy to origin
    url.pathname = url.pathname.replace('/lite','');
    return fetch(new Request(url.toString(), event.request));
  }
  return fetch(event.request);
});
```

Ravi (eng-auth): Ah — you're creating a new Request with event.request but using `url.toString()` — that can lose the full query in some edge runtimes if you don't pass the original `event.request`'s body/headers explicitly. Also some proxies limit header length; but more likely the issue is `fetch(new Request(url.toString(), event.request))` — if the runtime canonicalizes the URL it might drop or truncate long query params. Try `const proxied = new Request(event.request); proxied.url = url.toString();` — though setting url isn't standard. Better approach is `fetch(new Request(url.href, {method: event.request.method, headers: event.request.headers, body: event.request.body, redirect: 'manual'}))`.

Sean (Acme): Good call. We'll try that. Any quick workaround so production users don't get blocked?

Leah (security): Short-term: configure Google OAuth redirect to use a shorter state (reduce nonce length) — not ideal. Better: encode state as a compressed token (HMAC of session id) so it's under typical proxy limits. But that's a code change.

Maya (support): Also recommend adding a health-check route for OAuth flow that bypasses the worker for `/auth/callback` or use a rewrite rather than creating a new Request. E.g., let origin handle the `lite` path by letting request through and modifying headers — don't reconstruct URL.

Sean (Acme): We patched worker to forward full request like you suggested and retested — Google forwarded full state and auth succeeded locally. Rolling change to prod now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by Sean — deployment 2026-03-15T09:42:00Z (job #8421)

Ravi (eng-auth): For long-term, add a test in our auth integration suite that hits the edge path with a 256-char state to catch regressions. Also consider switching to a cookie-backed state where only a short ID is in query.

Leah (security): FYI: if you ever have `SameSite=None` cookies or cross-site redirects, confirm cookie flags and that the proxy preserves Set-Cookie headers for the domain. Not related to state truncation but common cause of `invalid_grant` in similar cases.

Sean (Acme): Rollout looks good so far — thanks team. Can you leave the thread open for 24h to confirm no more user reports?

Maya (support): Will do. Marking as **workaround applied** and engineering follow-up for long-term fixes (unit + integration tests, compressed state tokens). If anything pops up ping @Maya. :thumbsup:

Ravi (eng-auth): Adding ticket to auth backlog: `EDGE-4273` — reproduce with CF workers, add test and safe encoding suggestion.

Sean (Acme): Great, appreciate the quick turnaround :rocket:

Maya (support): Closing in 24h unless new reports.
